rows.what: Kurt and the Leibholz brothers in Berlin — THREE numbered asks: (1) Gertrud Leibholz née Leibke's death entry of 27 February 1943, (2) the Leibholz/Luwinski marriage of 5 January 1924 AND the date of the later divorce, with a question about a Landgericht divorce file, (3) Kurt Luwinski's 1912 birth entry and its Randvermerke. Full text now saved at requests/sent/2026-09-14-landesarchiv-berlin-SENT.txt.
rows.outcome: ANSWERED IN PART ON 29 SEPTEMBER, free of charge, by Ms Arabella Oberle (Recht und Benutzung), on a new thread (1a0ec4173f73cd37). SENT: scans of Gertrud Leibholz's death entry (Standesamt Wedding, P Rep. 830 Nr. 114) and of the Leibholz/Luwinski marriage entry (Schöneberg II, P Rep. 161 Nr. 171, Nr. 6/1924), whose margin records that the marriage was dissolved by a judgment of the Landgericht Berlin final on 21 March 1940 and that Jacob had to take the name Israel. NOT SENT: Kurt's 1912 birth entry. The 1912 registers are not digitised and she needs the Standesamt, which this archive had worked out on 20 September and never sent; the reply that supplies it is drafted (letter 39). The collective file holds only the 1923 banns papers and is not digitised; copies are a paid order through the Digitaler Antrag. A supplement drafted on 20 September was never sent and is overtaken.

rows.outcome: *** ANSWERED, AND IT IS A YES. *** IU.631.434.2026, dated 22 September 2026, signed by the Director KAROLINA KAWCZYŃSKA, case officer dr MAŁGORZATA URBANOWSKA-CHYŁA. The reply says the digital copies of the BIRTH, MARRIAGE AND DEATH registers of URZĄD STANU CYWILNEGO SZUBIN MIASTO “have already been made available some time ago” on www.genealogiawarchiwach.pl, and supplies a direct link to THE BIRTH REGISTER FOR 1884 — the year Jacob Leibholz was born at Schubin on 8 August. It explains how to expand the table of contents on the black bar to the left, and says the scan of any record found may be downloaded straight from the portal. NO FEE, NO QUERY SERVICE, NO ACKNOWLEDGEMENT REQUESTED — unlike the Koszalin reply, this one asks for nothing back. THE CONTRAST WITH KOSZALIN IS THE WHOLE POINT: the Hammerstein registers are gone and the Szubin ones were online the entire time this archive was writing letters about them. || *** SECOND ANSWER, 25 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND IT ANSWERS ALL THREE QUESTIONS. *** IU.631.434.2026, Director KAROLINA KAWCZYŃSKA, officer dr MAŁGORZATA URBANOWSKA-CHYŁA. (1) THE JEWISH REGISTERS OF SZUBIN SURVIVE, 1820-1847 ONLY — wrong span for Friederica b. c.1852, RIGHT SPAN FOR ABRAHAM SCHMUL b. 1846. (2) DEATH INDEXES SURVIVE 1874-1878 AND 1894-1924 AND NOTHING ELSE ('wyłącznie'), so 1879-1893 is a stated gap; they attached sygn. 246, the 1894-1908 volume, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAD PUBLISHED AS NON-EXISTENT. (3) AND THE SMALL FAVOUR PAID BEST: an archivist read the 'Tochter der...' line — 'GASTWIRTH JUDA I JUTTA Z DOMU MACHOL SCHMUL JEGO ŻONA'. FRIEDERICA'S FATHER KEPT AN INN, and the mother is read JUTTA née MACHOL against the index's JETTE MACHOT.
rows.acknowledged: Not required — the letter asks for no confirmation of receipt.
rows.followup: SECOND LETTER SENT 22 September 2026 on the IU.631.434.2026 thread, message 1a0c8d2a92207d0f: asks directly whether Bydgoszcz holds the akta gminy wyznaniowej żydowskiej w Szubinie, since Friederica Schmul was born about 1852 and Prussian civil registration began only on 1 October 1874. Text at requests/sent/2026-09-22-bydgoszcz-jewish-registers-SENT.txt. || THIRD LETTER SENT 27 September 2026 on the same thread, message 1a0e23f9d737321a, cc sdonczyk@: corrects two errors this archive put in their case file — the marriage is 24 DECEMBER not November, and the reading WILHELMINE is withdrawn — admits that the 'no alphabetical death index' claim was wrong and why, and asks whether an equivalent index survives for 1874-1893. *** IT WAS SENT BEFORE THEIR OWN ATTACHED LETTER HAD BEEN READ, AND THAT LETTER ALREADY ANSWERS THE INDEX QUESTION. *** Text at requests/sent/2026-09-27-bydgoszcz-correction-SENT.txt.

rows.what: Czarne (Hammerstein) civil registers 1847 and 1884, and the synagogue books — the Leibholz family
rows.outcome: ANSWERED IN FIVE LINES AND IT IS A NEGATIVE. O-S.6342.406.2026, signed by Krzysztof Skrzypiec, Head of the Slupsk Branch. The Koszalin holdings contain NO registers of the former German civil registry office at Czarne (Standesamt Hammerstein, Kreis Schlochau) FOR 1874 TO 1899, and NO synagogue-community books for Czarne AT ALL — and no information about what became of either, or where they might now be held. *** ACKNOWLEDGED 17 SEPTEMBER, message 1a0ac71a500bc77f, in their own thread 1a0a98796538c64b, to slupsk@ as they asked and copied to the case officer. The acknowledgement tells them WHY a negative was useful — that it closes the only route to Georg Leibholz’s parents — thanks them specifically for saying they do not know where the books went, and closes the correspondence so they need not spend more time on it.

rows.ackNote: ANSWERED, and it is an invitation to apply. Mr Keyster: "Please, apply for copies. Application form is attached. Please, submit proof of payment and the application on groundfloor." Two things his reply does not give: whether an applicant in Australia may submit by email rather than in person, and the fee and banking details. Both have to be asked. REPLIED 15 September asking the two things his message left out: whether an applicant in Australia may submit by email rather than in person, and the fee and banking details for the required proof of payment. The reply also states plainly, in advance, that David is not a relative and makes no claim on either estate — so that a standing objection comes before the fee rather than after it.

rows.what: Leonard's UDF service record and medal rolls — FOLLOWED UP 16 Sep with force number 141272, Corporal, POW
The parish marriage register of 7 September 1940
rows.outcome: *** ANSWERED IN FULL, IN A WEEK, AND THE ANSWER ON PARENTS IS NO. *** Arlene at the parish office replied to all five numbered questions. The 1940 parish marriage register SURVIVES and CONTAINS the entry; it DOES NOT NAME THE PARENTS — “Unfortunately not, as attached”. There is no second book: “the Catholic Church keeps one Marriage Register, the banns are included in the attached”, so the Original Marriage Register no. 13 of 1940 IS the parish register. Fr W. P. Whelan confirmed as parish priest at Rosebank from 1935, so the parish is the right one; the registers are held there, not at the Archdiocese. THIS CLOSES ROUTE 2 OF THE TWO ROUTES TO LEONARD'S PARENTAGE. A pure thank-you was sent the same day, message 1a0c8d21508292fb — no further request, because she answered everything asked.
rows.acknowledged: Thanks sent 22 September 2026, message 1a0c8d21508292fb, on the same thread.

drafts.who: Landesarchiv Berlin — Ms Oberle, answering her reply of 29 September
drafts.what: Thanks her, and supplies the one fact she said was missing: the Standesamt for Kurt Luwinski's 1912 birth, Berlin VIII, entry 963, with the reasoning so that she can check it. Adds Gertrud Leibholz's maiden name for her register, confirms what the divorce note settles, and asks one question before a paid order of the 1923 banns papers: whether they usually include both parties' birth certificates. Places no order. German.
drafts.note: FIRST. Reply on her thread of 29 September (a new thread, not the one of 14 September). A named archivist has been waiting since the 29th for the one fact she asked for, and it opens the route to Kurt's birth entry. The birth entry itself is then ordered through the Digitaler Antrag (work list row 226), which costs money and is David's. Delete the older draft of 20 September in the mailbox.

drafts.note: SECOND. Reply on your own thread of 14 September (mail thread 1a0a17e3f001a60d). That letter asked for the wrong year, so a search of the 1865 to 1934 books would find nothing, and it has had no answer in 33 days. It costs nothing to send.

drafts.who: Paul, a DNA match — corrections to the message of 16 September

drafts.note: THIRD. Reply on the MyHeritage thread. A correction to something already sent goes before any new request. Rewritten on 17 October; the earlier text carried 1916 and an 'exact' 1863.

drafts.what: An addition to the letter of 14 September about Kurt and the Leibholz brothers, naming the compensation files as a new subject. German.
drafts.note: FOURTH. Straight after 39, as a reply on the same thread of 29 September, so it reaches the same case officer. This is the highest-value document in the Kurt backlog: a compensation file holds the claimant's own sworn account of his life before emigration, which is the largest gap in his biography. Free digitisation of up to ten files a year may apply and the letter leaves that to them. Expect a form to shorten the protection period. Corrected on 17 October: Kurt's emigration year is stated as open, and Jacob's last address is Treuchtlingerstraße 4.

drafts.what: Asks for the marriage entry of Frederico Pinto da Rocha and Ivone, Lourenço Marques, 18 November 1939, which should name the parents of both and so open Frederico's family, and for Henrique's birth entry of 11 March 1941, which should name his father. Asks what proof of kinship is needed for a record under a hundred years old. Portuguese, with an English translation beneath.
drafts.note: FIFTH. A new correspondent; send on its own thread. Check the address at irn.justica.gov.pt first: the email held for this office comes from 2017 to 2018 listings. The quickest route for Henrique's birth may be for Derrick to sign the request himself, since he is the half-brother. Certificates are paid, and the fee is yours to decide.

drafts.what: Asks the national card index of compensation claims about four people of the LUWINSKI and LEIBHOLZ family. It exists because § 185 BEG decided WHICH Land’s authority was competent, and a Berlin-only enquiry can come back empty while the file sits elsewhere. German.
drafts.note: SIXTH. A new body and a new thread, sent on its own. It answers the question that comes before the Berlin one: whether Kurt, Auguste, Siegfried or Jacob filed at all, and with which authority. One enquiry covers all four, and a plain 'nothing on file' is a usable answer.

drafts.what: The East Prussian enquiry — the Allenstein and Kreis Rössel entries named by the Geneteka sweep. Polish.

It asks for the marriage of Joachim Luwinski and Johanna Thimm, the one line that would name Joachim's parents, the oldest generation of Kurt's mother's side this archive can reach. Polish. Bydgoszcz has answered every letter and sent a 76 MB volume unprompted, so it can wait for a good moment. Corrected on 17 October: it no longer calls Jacob Leibholz the father-in-law's grandfather.
